brief: Doctrine rewrite of 2026-08-21: every line is about the weather; the picture is the evidence. Three lines per photograph (Al’s ruled keeps locked and counted). Bank rescues marked. PAIRING-TASTE + the swap test still bind.
linesLabel: three per image incl. locked keeps

images.seen: A Nguni cow facing the camera on dew-heavy pasture, the rest of the herd and the trees fading into thick white fog. Tuesday.
lines: The herd is all here; the fog is just rationing them one at a time.
Visibility is down to one cow.
The farm goes on past that white wall; the cows are taking that on faith.

images.seen: A suburban street at blue pre-dawn with fog thickening down the road, three amber streetlamps fading into it, wet tar. Friday.
lines: Three streetlights in and the street gives up; the fog holds the rest.
The fog rolled in at three and started deleting the neighbourhood from the far end.
The streetlights are trying their best.

images.seen: A modern house at dawn with one warm-lit window cutting a long beam through dense fog, dark garden below. Wednesday.
lines: One lit window is taking on the whole fog, and losing beautifully.
The fog is thick enough to hold a beam of kitchen light like a solid object.
The morning forgot to render.

images.seen: A schoolboy in a hi-vis vest and backpack waiting at the curb, the street swallowed by fog, one faint pair of headlights deep in the mist. Monday.
lines: The hi-vis is doing exactly what it was bought for this morning.
Those headlights have been 'almost here' for two full minutes of fog.
Fog like this turns every school run into an act of faith and reflective tape.

images.seen: A runner on a wet forest road, the tall gum trees rising and disappearing into fog overhead. Saturday.
lines: The trees go up about thirty metres and then just stop existing.
The forest is keeping its top half private this morning.
The road is the only thing committing to a direction this morning.

images.seen: A golf ball sitting in wet rough in close-up, a golfer with his bag fading into heavy fog behind it. Sunday.
lines: Found: one ball. The other three hundred metres of golf course are still missing.
The fairway is out there somewhere, taking the morning off from being visible.
Fog gives every golfer the same handicap, and today it is generous.

images.seen: A tabby cat sitting on a brick garden wall, two ghostly human figures deep in the fog behind it, a Victorian house barely visible. Monday.
lines: The cat can see exactly what is in that fog and is choosing not to say.
The neighbours are out there somewhere, at about ten percent opacity.
Silent Hill vibes. Without the monsters. Hopefully.

images.seen: A Land Rover with headlights blazing on a misty lowveld road at dusk, acacia trees in layered fog, wet tar. Monday.
lines: The bushveld has gone soft-focus and the Landy is taking it slowly.
Headlights do about twenty metres out here; the rest is memory and respect.
Mist off the veld at dusk: the road home just doubled in length.

images.seen: An estate street at dusk swallowed by fog, one pair of red tail lights glowing deep in the mist, a single streetlight overhead. Thursday.
lines: Those brake lights are the only warm colour left in the neighbourhood.
The fog swallowed the whole street and left the tail lights as a receipt.
Home is two hundred metres away and completely theoretical right now.

images.seen: A woman walking a labradoodle along a foggy seafront promenade at dusk, a curve of haloed streetlamps fading into the mist. Tuesday.
lines: Every streetlamp gets its own halo tonight; the fog is generous like that.
The sea is somewhere just off to the right; you'll have to take it on hearsay.
The dog knows this route with its nose, which tonight is the better instrument.

images.seen: Two friends taking a smiling selfie at a lookout whose view is a wall of white fog, the sign beside them blanked out by mist. Sunday.
lines: The viewpoint is performing at zero percent and the selfie is happening anyway.
Somewhere behind all that white is a famous view. Allegedly.
The fog got to the lookout first and took the whole view for itself.

images.seen: An aerial view of Cape Town at night with fog rolling through the CBD, the city lights glowing amber through the mist, Table Mountain black above it all. Wednesday.
lines: Cape Town is still on under there; the fog is just running interference.
The sea mist came in for the night and the whole city went soft.
Table Mountain kept its head out; the city took the blanket.

images.seen: A minibus-taxi rank at night in fog — two white taxis under the depot lights, wet tar reflecting, two figures walking into the mist. Monday.
lines: Last taxis of the night, and the fog has the whole rank to itself soon.
The rank lights are punching holes in the fog, one bay at a time.
Wet tar, white air: the last leg home is the slow one tonight.

images.seen: A man walking up his garden path at night in thick fog, the kitchen window throwing one gold beam across the mist. Saturday.
lines: The kitchen light found him halfway up the path, which is what it is for.
The fog followed him right up to the gate and stopped at the window's beam.
That one window is doing lighthouse duty tonight, and it is enough.

images.seen: A traffic light in dense night fog, all three colours glowing as haloes at once over a wet empty intersection. Tuesday.
lines: The fog is so thick even the robot is hedging its bets.
Nobody is coming through that white, but the robot keeps performing anyway.
The intersection is running on trust and thirty metres of visibility.

images.seen: A man in a coat walking down the middle of a misty suburban street at night, one big haloed streetlight overhead. Thursday.
lines: The street is his alone tonight; the fog bought out every other pedestrian.
One streetlight is doing moon duty for the whole block.
Everything looks like a film scene. A creepy one.

images.seen: A farm dirt road lined with gum trees at golden foggy sunrise, frost on the verges, the farmhouse faint in the mist. Thursday.
lines: The sun is coming through the fog at half strength and full gold.
The mist gets the farm; the frost gets the verges; the road splits the difference.
This gold lasts exactly as long as the fog does, which is the deal.

images.seen: Three Nguni cattle standing at a wooden fence above a valley banked with fog, golden hills beyond, dew-heavy grass. Sunday.
lines: The fog filled the valley overnight; the Ngunis are standing on its shoreline.
Fog settles in the low ground, which is why the herd sleeps on the hill.
Three Ngunis watching the fog like it owes them a field.

images.seen: An empty rugby field in fog at first light, the near posts sharp and the far posts almost gone, houses ghosted behind. Saturday.
lines: Kickoff is ten and the far posts have not arrived yet.
The field is regulation size; you just have to take that on faith today.
Saturday rugby waits for the fog, and the fog is in no hurry.

images.seen: A man driving slowly through white-out fog, phone GPS mounted on the dash showing the route, mirror and glass hazed. Thursday.
lines: The GPS says the road is there, and today that is the whole case for it.
Twenty in a sixty and completely correct about it.
The phone knows the route; the fog is testing how much he trusts it.

images.seen: The Bo-Kaap at foggy dusk — pink, teal and yellow houses glowing under wall lamps, wet cobbles, a man watering his pot plants, the city fading into mist below. Friday.
lines: The fog took the city but it is not getting the Bo-Kaap's colours.
The whole city has gone grey below; this street refused, on principle.
The mist gets thicker downhill, and the houses get louder to compensate.

images.seen: A couple walking their bicycles down a foggy oak-lined lane at dusk, lamplight in the mist, wet leaves underfoot, white Cape Dutch gables behind. Wednesday.
lines: Too misty to ride, which neither of them minds in the slightest.
The fog turned the ride home into a walk, and the walk is better.
Mist in the oaks, gables in the mist: the Boland doing its winter thing.

images.seen: A foggy harbour jetty at dusk — moored yachts ghosted in the mist, jetty lamps glowing, a warm-lit restaurant at the end, an oystercatcher on the wet sand. Saturday.
lines: Every boat is staying exactly where it is, and the fog approves.
The masts have gone to silhouettes and the restaurant has gone to gold.
Nothing sails in this; even the oystercatcher is walking.

images.seen: A woman wrapped in a blanket with a steaming mug on her apartment balcony at night, the fog below glowing with soft streetlights. Sunday.
lines: The city noise is off tonight; fog is the best soundproofing there is.
The streetlights have gone soft and the whole suburb has gone quiet.
Fog outside, blanket outside too: some weather is for watching from one metre away.

images.seen: A couple walking a golden retriever at night through amber sodium fog, haloed streetlights, an art-deco apartment block glowing behind. Friday.
lines: The whole street has gone amber tonight; the fog is holding the light like syrup.
Friday night fog: the block gets quieter, the streetlights get bigger.
The fog moved in an hour ago and the streetlights have doubled in size since.

images.seen: A woman in a fleece walking her dog into thick ground fog — the taut leash disappears into the white and the dog is completely invisible. Tuesday.
lines: The dog is definitely still on the end of that leash. Almost definitely.
The leash goes into the fog and only faith comes back out of it.
Current visibility: one whole dog short of complete.

images.seen: A man in a gown and slippers wheeling his bin down the driveway into heavy fog, garden topiary fading behind him. Friday.
lines: Gown, slippers, thirty metres of visibility: bin day waits for no weather.
The bin run is being flown on instruments this morning.
Walking to the bin is now an expedition.

images.seen: A view over suburban rooftops with fog lying between the houses at golden sunrise, a jacaranda in bloom below, sun breaking through the layer. Wednesday.
lines: The fog is lying in the streets like it pays rates here.
Sun from above, fog from below: the suburb is the middle of the sandwich.
The fog got in among the houses overnight and the sun is evicting it street by street.
